tldr: A rare intervention attempt can be informative even when the state does not change. For the explicitly defined two-state rare-action triangular experiment, retaining all attempts and retaining only labelled state changes lead to distinct finite-information marked-process experiments for the stationary policy-value contrast. The theorem package proves strictly different all-procedure minimax squared risks for every interior public tuple, certifies a benchmark gap exceeding \(1/500\), transfers both risks and attaining procedures to the original dependent trajectory, and supplies a terminating compiler of arbitrarily accurate certified minimax brackets and total rules while preserving random occupations, terminal residence, the no-jump atom, and overflow.
gap: Average-reward policy evaluation supplies regular efficiency and distributional results, while statistical reduction supplies general decision ordering. Neither inspected theory determines the fixed-target minimax penalty of erasing unsuccessful opportunities when the logging probability is \(c/n\). A positive Bayes improvement at a convenient prior would leave this penalty unresolved.
fill: Target-specific conditional failed-count information supports a strict comparison over the complete parameter box. Separate estimator and prior certificates give a numerical benchmark without an asserted optimal prior support. A finite decision program, equipped with certified path probabilities and parameter-free reconstruction, turns both limit risks into arbitrarily accurate computable quantities and total rules on the original records.
